AI 2027, checked · as of November 15, 2026

Checkpoint 2026

In April 2025, AI 2027 told the story of the next two years month by month, and put numbers on most of it. We split its claims for 2025 and 2026 into 62 predictions, decided what would count as each one coming true, and checked them against what has happened since.

01May to August 20259 predictions

Mid 2025: Agents Arrive, Scores Lag

The scenario opens modestly, with agents that use a computer the way a person does, cost a lot and fail often enough to be a running joke.

Two footnotes put numbers on them: 65% on OSWorld and 85% on SWE-bench Verified.

The products kept to the timetable. The scores did not. Both came within 5 points of their targets — one at the end of September, the other in late November, and that one by Anthropic’s own count.

6 predictions

  1. The scenario’s story begins with the way these agents are advertised:

    “Advertisements for computer-using agents emphasize the term “personal assistant”: you can prompt them with tasks like “order me a burrito on DoorDash” or “open my budget spreadsheet and sum this month’s expenses.””

    AI 2027, Mid 2025 ↗

    What happened OpenAI launched ChatGPT agent on July 17, 2025, an assistant that works on a computer of its own. The launch post’s sample errand was to plan and buy the ingredients for a Japanese breakfast for four.

    Our callHappened, and on schedule. The pitch was older than the product, though — Operator, a research preview from January 2025, was already pitched with grocery orders before the scenario was published.

    AI 2027, Mid 2025 ↗

    What happened In July 2025, OpenAI’s Pro plan and Anthropic’s top Max plan each cost $200 a month, and each came with the company’s best agent tools.

    Our callHappened, at the very bottom of “hundreds”. Whether a $200 plan with an agent existed before April 2025, we have not checked.

Late 2025: The Cluster We Can’t Count

In the scenario, the leading lab spends late 2025 building the biggest data centers the world has seen.

Who plays the scenario’s OpenBrain? As 2025 ended, OpenAI, with the best public model on Epoch AI’s capability index.

Of the footnote’s three numbers for its data centers, only the power has a public figure, and that one is OpenAI’s own. How many chips the buildings hold depends on which of them you credit to OpenAI, and nobody has published what they cost.

Elsewhere the scenario did better than its numbers. A model of the size it named did arrive, if late, the rivals stayed close behind, and labs flagged their own public models as capable enough at hacking or biology to set off their safety rules.

    Our callCan’t be judged. Nothing public says which of those sites OpenAI really uses.

03January to April 202610 predictions

Early 2026: Nearly a Trillion

In the scenario, early 2026 is when the bet on automating AI research starts to pay off.

It also has the leading lab worth a trillion dollars. The leader on Epoch AI’s index, OpenAI, was valued at $852 billion when its funding round closed in March 2026, by SiliconANGLE’s report.

Most of the season went that way, near the scenario’s numbers and a little off them: more staff than it gave the leader, a power figure from one modeled dataset just over its line, and Anthropic’s own hacking scores either side of its range. Rivals did catch the leader, as it said they would.

Then there is the number the whole story turns on — AI making the leader’s research 50% faster — and no lab publishes it.

04May to August 202613 predictions

Mid 2026: Six Months Behind, No Takeover

In the scenario, mid 2026 is when China wakes up.

Short of chips, the scenario’s China nationalizes its AI research, pools half its computing power in one collective and builds a central zone at the Tianwan nuclear plant.

The lag it gives China held: on Epoch AI’s capability index, the one measure behind that verdict, Moonshot AI’s best model matched in late May 2026 what Anthropic had released 6.2 months earlier. The chips are far harder to see, and none of the six predictions about them can be judged.

And the state steps? None has been seen, and the reporting describes something closer to the opposite.

1 prediction

  1. Of China’s best labs, the scenario says they do a lot with little:

    “A few standouts like DeepCent do very impressive work with limited compute, but the compute deficit limits what they can achieve without government support, and they are about six months behind the best OpenBrain models.”

    AI 2027, Mid 2026 ↗

    What happened Every pairing of a leading US lab with a leading Chinese one fell inside our range of 4.5 to 7.5 months at some point between February and November 2026.

    Our callHappened. The gap moves whenever a new model comes out, and by August 31 it had shrunk to about 3 months.

  1. China’s share of compute, and its chips’ age

    China, in the scenario, gets by on smuggled, old and home-made chips:

    “By smuggling banned Taiwanese chips, buying older chips, and producing domestic chips about three years behind the U.S.-Taiwanese frontier, China has managed to maintain about 12% of the world’s AI-relevant compute—but the older technology is harder to work with, and supply is a constant headache.”

    AI 2027, Mid 2026 ↗

  2. What happened That is Epoch AI’s chip-owner data, down from 10.3% in mid-2025. Both figures count Epoch’s estimate of smuggled chips, a model Epoch calls speculative and leaves out of its own chart by default. Without it, the December share is 5.7%. Epoch’s overview page says “about 10%” of the computing delivered since 2022, a rounded summary of the same data.

    Our callCan’t be judged until the 2026 data arrive.

05September to December 202619 predictions

Late 2026: Some of It Came Early

We are writing in the middle of this one.

Two of its predictions came true before the months began. The Pentagon began contracting directly with the leading labs in June 2025, about 15 months ahead of the scenario, and Nvidia said in January 2026 that its Rubin chips were in full production.

The rest is a race against the calendar: Anthropic, top of Epoch’s index today, is on pace for the scenario’s revenue, the stock market is behind, and the cheap models are cheaper than it said.

Some of it no amount of waiting will settle — nobody measures turmoil in a job market, or what the managers of AI agents earn.

2027 and afternot graded

What the Scenario Says Comes Next

Here the scenario stops being checkable and starts being the point. In January 2027 its leading lab trains Agent-2 without pause, and the new model roughly triples the pace of the lab’s research. In February, the scenario’s China steals the weights. By March, AI-made breakthroughs produce Agent-3, a superhuman coder, and in July the lab declares AGI and sells a cheap version to the public. In September Agent-4 becomes a superhuman AI researcher, and falls under suspicion of being misaligned; in October a leaked memo sets off a public backlash and government oversight.

And after that? The story splits into two endings, a race and a slowdown, for the reader to choose. None of it is graded here — its months have not come.
